newsitem.title: CANADA: IIMA chief urges cooperation among Asian nations.
newsitem.headline: IIMA chief urges cooperation among Asian nations.

text.p: President of the Institute for International Monetary Affairs in Tokyo, Toyoo Gyohten, said on Saturday that Japan seeks cooperation with other East Asian nations to stimulate the region's economy and to avoid hegemony by any one nation.
"Japan is neither able to nor desirous to become a hegemonic power in Asia," said Gyohten, a former Vice Minister of Finance for International Affairs in Japan. "We know our limitations."
But Gyohten told delegates in Toronto for the 39th annual congress of the Association Cambiste International that Japan should not stand idly by while other nations seek hegemony in the region.
"What Japan hopes for and believes in is to be a partner in stimulating and supporting development and in sharing the benefits of common achievement," he said.
Gyohten told delegates that there were several principles that East Asian nations should stand by as they promote the regional economic development.
He said nations should be reminded that East Asia's development has been made possible by "mutual stimulation" in an open environment.

He urged East Asian nations to make continual efforts to avoid becoming adversarial in their dealings and to acknowledge the constant battles to reach compromise that at the same time recognized the region's diversity.

Gyohten said the region's nations must expand human and cultural exchanges for the development of multinational projects and must continue to point out examples that prove economic interdependence generated mutual benefits.
"East Asia is full of possibilities but it is also full of risks," Gyohten said.
